title: Run-rate sensitivity grid: on-prem vs dedicated mix (Q3 2026)
summary: Working workbook-style analysis exploring run-rate implications of shifting % of customer demand from hosted to on-prem (private) and dedicated reserved capacity. Includes headcount phasing, unit-cost sensitivity bands, and trigger rules for temporary surge credits or contractor pools.
content:
Purpose:
This is a lightweight run-rate sensitivity grid to help the finance and infra teams decide: for a given product mix shift toward on-prem / private deployments and dedicated capacity, what are the expected impacts on monthly cash burn, hiring windows, and break-even price adjustments. Draft for Q3 planning; assumptions below are intentionally conservative and meant to be debated, not gospel.

High-level framing:
- Problem: Customers ask for on-prem/private deployments (higher margin products) but those require more upfront engineering and professional services headcount, and often reduce hosted usage (token revenue). We need a reproducible sensitivity grid to weigh tradeoffs across hires, contract costs, and price guards.
- Goal: Produce triggerable guardrails (pricing increases, temporary surge credit usage, hiring approvals) if run-rate moves against baseline.

Key assumptions (baseline):
- Baseline product mix (today): Hosted API 78%, Dedicated 15%, Private/on-prem 7% of revenue.
- Scenario range modeled: Private share increases from 7% -> 7/15/25/40% (four scenarios). Dedicated changes complement private (we model both shifting).
- Avg revenue per customer-month (ARPCM): Hosted $1,200; Dedicated $5,000 (committed); Private deal average $28,000 (professional services + infra + license).
- Incremental staff needs for private deals: 0.15 FTE per $100k ARR (customer success + solutions eng + security onboarding) frontloaded over Q0–Q3 of deal; plus 0.02 FTE ongoing for support.
- Average fully-burdened engineer cost (finance): $240k/year; solutions engineer/prof-services: $190k/year; contractor apron: $120k/year equivalent (short-term).
- On-prem one-time engineering uplift per deal (average): $60k (SWE + infra + security).
- Hosted unit token cost (cloud + GPU): $0.00009 per token average; reserved/dedicated unit cost (after utilization) equivalent to $0.00005 per token. Private is large one-time margin plus lower per-token in customer but more fixed GTM/PS costs.

Tabular run-rate outputs (monthlyized):
Columns: Scenario / Private % / Dedicated % / Net new hires (quarter) / Monthly cash delta vs baseline / Required price uplift on hosted % to preserve gross margin
- Baseline: Private 7% / Dedicated 15% / Net new hires Q3: +3 FTE (mix: 2 SE, 1 CSM) / Monthly delta: +$0 / Hosted price uplift: 0%
- Scenario A (moderate): Private 15% / Dedicated 18% / Net new hires Q3: +8 FTE (4 SE, 2 SRE infra, 2 CSM) / Monthly delta: +$210k / Hosted price uplift needed: +5%
- Scenario B (material shift): Private 25% / Dedicated 20% / Net new hires Q3: +18 FTE (8 SE, 4 infra, 6 CSM/solutions) / Monthly delta: +$520k / Hosted price uplift needed: +12%
- Scenario C (strong enterprise push): Private 40% / Dedicated 25% / Net new hires Q3: +35 FTE / Monthly delta: +$1.05m / Hosted price uplift needed: +25%

Breakdown notes: monthly delta is primarily driven by frontloaded PS/SE hiring and one-time uplift amortized, plus ongoing incremental account management. Dedicated revenue is sticky and offsets some per-token hosted erosion but increases reserved GPU capex commitments (if Redwood backs infra) or reduces hosted throughput in favor of dedicated pools.

Sensitivity bands (what moves the numbers):
- Faster PS automation (tooling) reduces per-deal SE load from 0.15FTE->$0.08FTE, materially lowering hires required.
- Increased pricing on private deals (higher professional services margins) reduces cash delta.
- If hosted token mix falls >10% faster than modeled, cash delta increases by ~15–20% due to lost incremental hosted margin.
- Contractor utilization: using contractors for first 3 months saves ~45% of first-quarter cash vs hiring (but increases operational risk).

Triggering policy (proposed):
- If monthly delta > $300k sustained for 6 weeks, pause new mid/senior SWE hires (freeze) and prioritize contractors for immediate bandwidth.
- If private mix forecast > 20% AND candidate pipeline for SE roles < 6 strong candidates, raise hosted price by 8% for new signups only and introduce a 3-month implementation surcharge for private deals.
- Auto-burst credit: allocate a one-time surge credit bucket (up to $250k funded from ops contingency) to be used to smooth customer migration windows; usage requires CFO + Head of Sales signoff.

Quick scenario chart (verbal):
- Low-volume shift (to 15% private): manageable with contractor apron + +8 hires; runway impact is modest and reversible.
- Mid-volume shift (25% private): requires deliberate hiring plan and pricing actions; recommend gating via a 2-week exec review and potential temporary hosted price uplift.
- High-volume shift (40% private): triggers a hiring funding round (defer non-essential projects) or immediate price reset.

Action items (next 30d):
1) Finance + Product to create a detailed per-deal PS build-up template (FIN-4123) — due 2026-07-09 — owner: Priya.
2) Infra + SRE to produce a tooling roadmap that can reduce SE onboarding FTE by 40% if delivered (MVP by 2026-10). Owner: @sofia-m.
3) Sales to flag pipeline deals expected to convert in next 3 months and annotate whether they are on-prem/private; deliver list by 2026-06-25.
4) Run a contractor vs hire cost test on 5 recent private deals and produce cold numbers; finance to model worst-case cash flow for Scenario B/C.

Open questions / debate points:
- Should Redwood absorb on-prem infra costs as part of product (slower payback but competitive advantage) or push those costs onto customers (faster margin recovery but higher sticker shock)?
- What is a defensible short-term hosted price uplift without materially harming PLG funnel? (We recommend gating to new accounts only).
- How aggressive should we be with automation investment vs hiring? Capex vs opex tradeoff.

Notes and references:
- See linked ticket FIN-4123 (detailed assumptions) and CONFLUENCE:FIN/RunRateMixGrid for the working model.
- Slack thread: #finance-capacity-discuss has early SRE -> finance notes.
- This doc is intentionally a working-sheet; expect numbers to change after SE tooling estimates and the sales pipeline feed.

Draft status: in_review — please comment inline in drive or ping Priya / Marcus.

(quick numbers/cheat): per new private $1m ARR bucket -> expected 0.15 FTE frontloaded = ~$3k/mo (amortized) baseline delta; useful for quick back-of-envelope when sizing deals.
